- **Source:** [GOG product page](https://www.gog.com/en/game/robin_hood)
- **Publisher / source author:** GOG / publisher-supplied product information
- **Language:** English
- **Original release:** 14 November 2002
- **GOG release:** 6 March 2012
- **Preservation changelog:** 25 April 2025
- **Developer / publisher:** Spellbound Entertainment AG / Microids
- **Access:** The product page is JavaScript-rendered; the product API supplied the duplicate description and product metadata.
- **Checked / retrieved:** 9 September 2026

## Product information

**Robin Hood: The Legend of Sherwood** is a single-player, DRM-free game for Windows. It is tagged **Strategy**, **Real-time**, **Tactical**, **Classic**, **Historical**, **Isometric**, **Medieval**, **Stealth**, and **Good Old Game**. The page lists a PEGI rating of 12+ for violence.

The page lists a 4.5/5 rating from 304 reviews and a HowLongToBeat estimate of 15 hours for the main story, 18 hours for main story plus sides, 18.5 hours for completionist play, and 17 hours for all styles.

GOG states that the game is part of its Preservation Program and is “2026-ready.” The page highlights Windows 11 verification, technical support, and lifetime maintenance. It also states that no activation or online connection is required to play.

## Description

England, Anno Domini 1190 – Richard the Lionheart is held prisoner and his brother, Prince John rules over the simple peasants with an iron hand and this pure force of arms forces them to bend to authority. Only one man takes up the struggle against the oppressors, supported by a small band of brave and loyal followers. His name; Robin Hood.

Roam the dense foliage of Sherwood, come face to face with royal trouble and battle against Prince John’s forces as you take on the role of legendary nobleman, Robin Hood. Team up with Little John and the rest of the Merry Men as the battle for the King’s throne ensues in this stealth-based, real-time strategy game.

### Key features

- Non-linear campaign system with over 30 different missions
- Mission types from Robbery and Infiltration to Castle Attack and Ambush
- Combines action and adventure with stealth tactical elements
- Innovative combat system, interact with the mouse while fighting to access special combat skills
- Play as Robin Hood, Little John, Friar Tuck or even Maid Marian, nine characters in all, each with specific abilities and attributes
- Spectacular graphics with realistic atmospheric conditions like day, night and fog
- Explore historic locations; Sherwood Forest, Nottingham Castle, York and many more

© 2011 Anuman Interactive. All rights reserved.

## GOG preservation changelog

### Changelog (25 April 2025)

- Fixed GOG GALAXY installers so your game actually installs (what a concept!) on modern PCs.
- Applied a DirectX Wrapper to make everything look and run better.
- Added new rendering options: Windowed Mode, V-Sync, Gamma Correction, Integer Scaling, Anti-Aliasing, and more.
- Validated stability (the only crash you might feel is pure nostalgia).
- Verified compatibility with Windows 10 and 11.
- Added Cloud Saves support.

## FAQ

### What operating systems is Robin Hood: The Legend of Sherwood compatible with?

Robin Hood: The Legend of Sherwood is officially supported on Windows.

### Does Robin Hood: The Legend of Sherwood have DRM?

No! GOG games have no DRM and can be played without an internet connection, totally offline. Some bonus content might require an internet connection to download, but we do our best to limit that need. [Read more about DRM.](https://www.gog.com/blog/preservation/drm-free/)

### Do you need GOG Galaxy to play Robin Hood: The Legend of Sherwood?

No! You do not need GOG Galaxy to play Robin Hood: The Legend of Sherwood. GOG gives you the option to download a fully offline installer and install Robin Hood: The Legend of Sherwood that way, without using GOG Galaxy. GOG Galaxy is used for synchronization of achievements and cloud saves, but its usage is totally optional. [Read more about GOG Galaxy.](https://www.gog.com/galaxy)

### What are the system requirements for Robin Hood: The Legend of Sherwood?

Minimum: System: Windows 10, Processor: 1.8 GHz, Memory: 2 GB RAM, Graphics: 3D graphics card compatible with DirectX 9.0c.

### ezcolm — “Playable on W11 / Playable on W11”

I will leave my review in two languages, Spanish and English.

Recently, to remember my childhood with these strategy-type games, I decided to play it again. The game ran on Windows 11 version 22H2 without any problems.

The only detail is in the mission to rescue Robin: there is a bug. The solution is in a Spanish Steam review. You must download some files and have the game in English; once the modification is made, load a save from before reaching that mission, enter the rescue mission, save the game, and then you can switch back to your preferred language and continue.

#### Old, nearly perfect, heaps of fun

**Pajdagog — July 26, 2026 — 5/5**
[GOG profile](https://www.gog.com/u/Pajdagog)

I consider myself something of a connoiseur, when it comes to isometric stealth tactical games. I started with original Commandos, I enjoy all of Shadow tactics games and also Desperados. Robin Hood is, at first glance, more primitive, with rather naive, albeit functional and cute graphics. But below it is unique and very satisfying. First of all, all the characters, both yours and NPC, have their own UI, often surprisingly complex, fluid and adapting to situation. When not selected, characters in your crew can still defend themselves, often surprisingly well. Not once I left Little John standing alone, and when returning, i found him standing among dozen of stunned opponents. 
Also, the game´s leaning towards hand to hand combat, instead of ranged, means much more combinations and tactics. The opponents are not uniformly killable/unkillable. Even a farmer with pitchfork can kill a mounted knight, with good timing and some luck. I am playing Legend of Sherwood for quarter of century now and I am still entertained. Five stars, no reservations.

#### Mediocre Commandos clone

**Handshakes — October 12, 2014 — 2/5**
[GOG profile](https://www.gog.com/u/Handshakes)

So I gave this game a tumble after reading all of the good reviews of it, but I must say that I just don't see it. 

At best, this game is a functional clone of Commandos. What that means is that It is an isometric squad based stealth action game. Unlike Commandos, it isn't incredibly unforgiving and hard. It is still quite difficult, mind you, but if you botch the stealth you can still get by on your sword swinging skills. I'd put that as one of the few positive points for the game.

What the game does particularly well is level design. Although you have a linear set of objectives for each level, how you choose to accomplish those objectives is completely up to you. You can stealth your way through, you can pick foes off from a distance, you can get them to fight eachother, or you can run in swords swinging. There are multiple paths to take, and multiple challenges to be met.

Going against the game is the appalling user interface. The mouse feels incredibly sluggish, and the entire game is controlled through click commands (there are esoteric keyboard shortcuts if you can figure them out). All in all, controlling this game is a mess and not at all a pleasure, and is the single worst aspect of this game.

The graphics hold up poorly, being from that era where everybody thought pre-rendered sprites looked good (they don't). The voice acting is virtually non-existent.

There is a story, told entirely through text, which just serves to give a tiny bit of context to the set of increasingly difficult scenarios that you have to run through.

All in all, I'd say avoid this game unless you REALLY love Commandos, Robin Hood, or both. Actually, if you love Robin Hood I'd recommend the much better "The Adventures of Robin Hood" from 1992. That game also controls like garbage (although it is much more forgivable, coming from a 1992 game), but has several innovative and unique gameplay elements, unlike this derivative mess.

#### Not good enough, I'm afraid

**pearnon — May 9, 2016 — 2/5**
[GOG profile](https://www.gog.com/u/pearnon)

I should have known better, having already purchased the game in my youth to get my Commandos fix and having gotten bored with it. Years later, I tried it again at GOG, again to scratch a Commandos itch, thinking I might be able to appreciate the game better, but alas, history repeated itself.

At face value, this is Commandos in the Middle Ages, but the story is cartoonish, as are the characters, the repetitive ambush missions are an irksome, frequent intermission between missions, and it's far too easy to slash your way through problems with some swordplay or staff swinging. It has the ingredients of a good game, but the whole just doesn't seem to gel together, and even the innovative features, like leaving your Merry Men in their training camp, becomes unwieldy and cumbersome after the novelty wears off. The fact that I had to use a third-party program so that the game was even playable (the infamous field of vision slowdown) didn't help at all. Not one of my finest purchases, and the lowest common denominator of a strategy game, I'm afraid.

#### Robin Hood - The Childhood of Sherwood

**MurusCZ — August 29, 2025 — 4/5**
[GOG profile](https://www.gog.com/u/MurusCZ)

Ok, so first things first. I am very much biased in this review as Robin Hood is a childhood memory from elementary school where evry computer had this game installed for some reason. And young me loved it. 

But its only when I found this as an adult that finally aprecciated the game fully. There has never been a better game depiction of Robin Hood and his Companions. Each one is distinct enough that you carry them with you every mission. Especially Brother Tuck is hilarious. though because every companion has a special ability, it makes the generic ones useless, unless you want meat for the grinder, or plan to skill up your special characters.

When it comes to mission design in many cases there is more than one way to get to where you need to be. There is only a few maps, so you will be revisiting them with new guard paths and new scroll quests. 

Sherwood is very homely as a base, thats it. Its usefulness is very much about making stuff for your characters or skilling them up in archery, slinging or melee combat.

The last thing I need to highlight is czech voicover and subtitles. Under CD Project many games got Czech localisation in many cases fully dubbed over. This was one of those games, and dubing even after years is more than decent. The same cant be really said about english though. Its floppy at best, boring at worst. It almost sounds like it was dubbed on couch at home.

And thats about it. I think this game is great to play through at least once. It may not be game you pick up again any time soon after beating it however. But as a product of its time, cinematics hold great, gameplay is easy to pick up, and story is more then decent.

#### Surprisingly fun once you get going

**Hannibalscipio — December 27, 2021 — 4/5**
[GOG profile](https://www.gog.com/u/Hannibalscipio)

By watching a couple of tutorials, I got the hang of this game pretty quickly. You complete missions and build your band of merry men. As the story advances, your camp economy flourishes (assuming you don't lose many merry men). This makes it easier to complete missions. There are a variety of fun abilities to use in missions.

Aside from a level that forces you to subdue all opponents with non-lethal force, the level design is mostly sound. Fighting mounted knights is the big problem - combat with them is glitchy. You also can't knock them out, so your only option is to stun them and then kill them - not my fighting mode of choice. Many of my mission restarts came because my characters couldn't figure out how to strike his area.

#### Robin Hood: Punch-Out Edition

**mdqp — May 21, 2026 — 4/5**
[GOG profile](https://www.gog.com/u/mdqp)

Robin Hood is Real-Time-Tactics game in the vein of Commandos and Desperados (the latter of which was created by the same developers). In fact, Robin Hood might very well be the real Desperados sequel, unlike Desperados 2.

Regardless, RH stands as a solid game on its own. The pre-rendered sprites and backgrounds are detailed and lively, music is nice, albeit a bit too repetitive (especially the "tense" music you hear when there is combat or you get discovered, as some times it keeps playing even when you think you resolved the fight). The sounds are also more than adequate. The narration isn't the strongest suit or focus of the game, but it adequately strings the campaign missions together, and it hits on some of the iconic moments in the Robin Hood legend.

Unlike most other games in the genre, you have a team of Merry Men on top of your named characters, allowing you to build your teams with a decent degree of freedom (the named characters though are generally better and have some unique abilities). If the mission requires a specific skill to be completed, the game will remind you of it when you assemble the team, so you don't have to worry about locking yourself out of completing the map.

You gain more "generic" Merry Men by avoiding bloodshed during missions, and the men you don't bring with you on missions have some uses like creating consumables back at the base camp, or they can be used as resources in some events that require assaulting certain cities (using the Merry Men, money or completing extra missions before those make things easier) or during defense events (which offer the same options, but aren't actual missions, just a "resource check" of sorts, which delays the game if you fail).

As for the meat of the game, you have a campaign made up of fixed missions, as well as some generic, repeatable ones (randomly made available for you at certain intervals). These generic ones aren't bad, actually, but the repetition does settle in eventually. Still, they are there as a release valve of sorts, as you'll need to gather money to advance the story at a certain point.

The real fun comes from the main missions, however. While those also re-use the maps, the different enemy placement, objectives and what not more than make up for the lack of diverse environments. Your team has pretty wide range of abilities and items, although some are much better than others (Little John being able to knock out stronger targets with one hit, for example, outshines Robin in most scenarios, especially if you want to keep the body count low). The maps are mostly well-designed and well-paced, with lots of additional objectives, treasures, interactions and so on (gather all the special items in the game for a bit of an extra at the end).

The game does have some issues in the gameplay department, however: your characters are pretty good in combat, which helps reduce frustration when things don't go according to plan, however this is also very exploitable. The AI isn't very bright at times, while at others it seems to be able to perceive you beyond its cone of vision (different heights and partial cover are also extremely annoying, as the game doesn't always do a good job at showing the cone in those situations). Some enemies are needlessly strong or unbeatable, slowing you down or forcing you to adopt the same tactics over and over, without adding much strategy. Some of the late maps have simply TOO many soldiers everywhere, which detracts from the experience. The final map also splits your party for no good reason, and the pairings are seemingly random, which might force you to kill tons of guards or exploit the AI if you don't want to "reroll". Archers are also a pain, as they can effectively stun lock you if you aren't careful. The game does give you some leeway with healing items or the ability to "resurrect" by consuming lucky clovers, and generally the game it's not TOO difficult, however executing a plan "cleanly" might be impossible, with how sensitive the AI is.

Still, the game is overall very fun, and the melee combat being more of a focus compared to other games in the genre gives this one its own unique identity. If you like this style of games, Robin Hood comes definitely recommended.

#### Started well, but got boring quickly!

**ironic_lettuce — November 11, 2017 — 3/5**
[GOG profile](https://www.gog.com/u/ironic_lettuce)

Having been a huge fan of the Commandos games, I thought I'd give Robin Hood a try as it was on sale, but sadly I feel this game isn't quite polished enough to merit any more than 3 stars, and certainly wouldn't recommend paying the full price for it. While I don't think it's a bad game by any means, I just think it falls well short of the standard that Commandos set. 

There is a huge sense of repetitiveness that comes from the raid missions that happen in between the main story missions, as they all occur over just 3 different maps. Once you've seen those maps multiple times, it gets really tedious. I actually resorted to using a cheat code to get through some of them because I was just so bored of them by that point.

And I just feel some of the characters have really useless abilities (like the apple throw) that meant I ended up using a few abilities from a few of the characters over and over. There were also occasions where I literally don't think there was a way to sneak past, and I was forced into combat, which I didn't like, as I enjoy playing these games in full stealth.

The main upside I feel is the graphics, which are beautifully hand drawn and really draw you into the game. I also like the mechanic of the Merry Men training, and upgrading of their skills.

Overall I'd say, if you're looking for a pure stealth strategy game, that you'd be best looking elsewhere. However, if not, this game could provide some hours of fun, but again I would wait till it's on sale!

#### Embarassing when compared to its peers

**Wormerine — March 4, 2015 — 2/5**
[GOG profile](https://www.gog.com/u/Wormerine)

I have a lot of nostalgia toward this game, though even as kid I felt the game was a bit garbage. And don’t get deceived by positive reviews. This game was released a year after Desperados, and apparently it was made by the same studio – but quality wise it is nowhere near the same level. UI is atrocious, enemies really static with unmoving vision cones, individual heroes really limited in what they can do, mechanics and rules poorly explained (if at all). Presentation took a real hit - the game opens up with couple rough text boxes to set up a scene with you character standing in the middle of the map. Not a great introduction and it doesn’t get better. It also lacks proper tutorials.

There are some ideas with potential – there is a bit of economy going on – generic units join you, if you don’t kill too many people and you can assign them to jobs back at the base – so they train, or produce consumables while you are on missions.

The game also has some performance isssues on modern systems. 

If you are into the genre of real-time tactics games it might be worth picking up for curiosity sake, but it’s not very fun or playable if you don’t have some thick nostalgia goggles.

**illiniorange — March 24, 2026 — 4/5**

Technical:
Reports all over the web say the retail version is basically unplayable on modern systems, yet I completed this version with exactly one crash and no other issues.  This  product is an example of GOG at its finest.

Gameplay:
The game strikes a nice balance of encouraging stealth without requiring it.  (The lower your body count, the more Merry Men will flock to Sherwood.  But you're unlikely to run out of Merry Men, so it's not worth sweating.)  I probably focused too much on stealth in my play, which not only renders Robin somewhat impotent (his greatest asset is his deadly bow) but makes some of the later missions either frustrating or just plain tedious.  (The last few mission require knocking out, binding, and hiding nearly the entire village if you're going for stealth.)  You might have more fun than I did if you're less focused on stealthy solutions to the later missions.

#### A Perfect Robin Hood

**darkovika — April 25, 2026 — 5/5**
[GOG profile](https://www.gog.com/u/darkovika)

This game is gorgeous. In the beginning, I always flounder a little as I get back into the groove, but once you figure out the best way to handle each level, you start getting really good and fast at it. 

The game is an isometric pixel art masterpiece. The music is phenomenal. You have Robin and your main crew, but you also have units that you can use throughout the game. During missions, you can set your other Merry Men to train, which can sometimes be a good idea and sometimes not. A character with nearly maxed out combat skills will almost certainly instantly kill a character... but if you're gunning for a high score, then you'll want to use your Merry Men with their blunt weapons to take out enemies, and raising their combat score might actually not be a good thing. It might even be better to put them all to working on creating items to take into missions, instead. 

There are so many things to do that just when you think you've figured out the core gameplay loop, something new will be thrown at you. You get all of the main points of Robin Hood and so much more.

It's one of my most favorite games. It can get a little repetitive at some point, but not every single side quest is required, a point worth remembering, as you can sometimes feel you're meant to do them all.

If you're playing easy, by the way, a heavy Merry Man can take you a LONG way, lol.

Oldy but goldy.

You have several main characters that are really done with details (from their abilities to their background and how you meet them).

The story is done well and there is no feeling of repetition due to different castles (maps), different tasks, different day times, different weather conditions that affect visibility...

There are lots of "side quests" that if you explore every map and every room (especially highly guarded),  you will find out about.

Long story short, I still pick this over any commandos game (and even Desperados).

#### One of the last great games of its genre

**T-Rexvs.Skenderbeg — February 12, 2019 — 5/5**
[GOG profile](https://www.gog.com/u/T-Rexvs.Skenderbeg)

One of the greatest tragedies of contemporary gaming is that games like this aren't being made anymore. When we had glorious, beautiful 2D maps instead of disgusting cartoonish 3D (although the character icons and some models in this game are kinda cartoonish in both voice and appearance, but hey, you can't have it all). Seriously, the maps in this game are so gorgeous I would have them painted as murals on the walls of my house if I knew anyone half-competent for the job (at least the half of the house I wouldn't do in Desperados map murals). There are some gripes to be had with it - the game rewards you for not killing enemies, rendering Robin Hood's bow and arrow pretty much useless, and the inability to choose your character's equipment means that Robin will have a non-lethal staff in the sherwood missions, and a lethal sword in the cities, again making the titular character the one you're least likely to use unless the game outright requires it of you. And the only reward you get for using the non-lethal approach is more useless generic merry men which fall into three types, only one of which being somewhat useful until you get Little John to join the gang. The only other use for the men is throwing them into the meat grinder once you get to the siege missions.

Most of the 1 and 2 star reviews for this game are just giving it shit for not being Commandos. Because what would you expect from a game about a medieval English folk-tale hero other than Commandos, right?

#### Great Game, Great Music, Great Game-play

**NomanJohan — October 23, 2014 — 5/5**
[GOG profile](https://www.gog.com/u/NomanJohan)

Man! People are gonna tell you how this is like a Commandos type game etc. but it's actually way more than that. It came from the makers of Desperados - a already better version of Commandos.

- Meele combat mechanism - only game of it's kind to have that
- Shielded enemy and crossbow firing from behind, Heavily armoured knights
- Hideout and small economy system for items
- Ambush Mechanism
- Great music
- Fun, cheesy plethora of dialogue from the character and enemies
- Difficulty settings can turn it into as unforgiving as the other games of this genre if not even harder
- More climbing and jumping from roof to roof
- Beautiful Medieval settings
- Has an interesting story
- Colourful characters and abilities
- The intro

Missed opportunity: They could add custom weapons/armour shop with the money system they introduced.

Overall an unique fun game, just get it please.

#### Still addictative after 20 years

**Dawwwg — January 7, 2024 — 5/5**
[GOG profile](https://www.gog.com/u/Dawwwg)

It does need a 3rd party patch to get it to run properly on modern Windows versions (google the games name + "lag fix"), but besides that, it runs just fine.   Given how old the game is (and how easy to fix), I didn't subtract that drawback from my rating.

Secondly make sure to not set too high a resolution or you'll miss out on all the beautiful graphical details and animations.

I'm also not sure why some reviewers complain about the missing tutorials, the 1st level has all the tutorial hints you need and the game is pretty forgiving about combat - assuming you actually follow the game hints.

All in all it aged pretty well, even the AI isn't bad, as enemies don't get stuck or lost; the gameis pretty addictive &amp; easy to pick up and more forgiving than (for example) Commando's and there's a lot of content; aka the value for money is very decent, even ignoring the huge discounts during sales on it.

**Jimthesfn — August 2, 2021 — 4/5**

I had no idea what to expect of the game. It was suggested to me and must say it was a wonderful experience.
You do have a choice if you want to be stealthy or not. Hide bodies or just leave them be. Kill or not to kill.
Every choice has it consequences thou. There are many ways to deal with enemies and also to trick them.

One thing that I didn't like is the forced "assaults" you have to do towards the end as they felt pointless at that point.

There are parts of a very few buildings you can't see behind which is annoying as there can be enemies standing there but you can't see that if they are not patrolling.

Something I really liked is the behaviour of the soldier enemies react if somebody is missing. Same thing with how some people will snitch on you by running to an enemy soldier or leader and tell on you.

Close combat is fun as you actually use the mouse to control the swing of your characters.

Enjoyed the game a lot and can easily recommend it.

#### Classic game well worth your money.

**lis200 — April 30, 2018 — 5/5**
[GOG profile](https://www.gog.com/u/lis200)

I remember playing this back in the day (wow now I sound like my dad...). This is a classic game, full of features and different way's to accomplish objectives. Not only that it has an excellent, albeit done to death, story. I think it was ahead of it's time. To be honest it has aged quite well. 

The game is very similar to Commando's. Each character has different abilities and assists in ways of sneaking, and smashing your way around the map to complete certain scenarios. There are main characters but also random characters that join with similar abilities to your main ones. This helps as in the downtime during missions you can assign people back at your base to construct things like traps and nets etc. 

It really was a cleverly designed game and back in the day when you did not get the chance to release a day one patch or the mass production of clone video games. A lot of care and love went into this one and I highly recommend it for 10 bucks, you will get excellent value for your time, i've replayed it more than once. 

This is my opinion however, as i do enjoy strategy rpg games. If you prefer the FPS route than you probably wont like this.

#### Tedious missions + clunky under Win10

**wongqc — May 1, 2020 — 3/5**
[GOG profile](https://www.gog.com/u/wongqc)

[What I loved]
I love its demo back when it was released.
Contrary to what some 1-star reviews say, you *can* knock out almost every single person, or at least not have any blood on your hands.  The mission rewards you for sparing lives.
If you're paired up with a fighter, have 1 engage your enemy, and use the un-engaged Merry-Man to knock him out.

[Difficult and Tedious Mission]
The missions can be hard, even on the tutorial mission.  You have to figure out that entering one door allows you multiple exits.  It's hard to know who you're supposed to meet inside "the castle", when they should have said "the keep". Once you're out of the castle, you face a line of footmen that you won't be able to sneak up on, so it's "throw money bags and punch the last guy standing".  Some save scumming would be required as he's not totally distracted.  This makes the first mission tedious.  Upon completion, I'm told that I didn't loot some 2000 gold pieces.  What?!  Shouldn't the tutorial handhold me on this?  I'm no interest in replaying that! 

[Realism]
After getting your head knocked in, should you call for a search?
Also, guards are pretty short sighted.

[Interface]
Checking guards' vision requires me to mouse-over the desired guard.

[Performance]
Very laggy on Win10, removing much enjoyment.

Base Game: 3/5
Current Laggy State: 2/5

I remember playing this game when I was younger and being instantly caught by it. Basically, it's just a Commandos game, with a few differences and easier difficulty. I was playing it in Russian, and I don't know jack Russian. That's how fun it was. 

You still had stealth elements, however the game was not as unforgiving if you failed as the other games of the same type (including Desperados).

I recommend this game to people as myself, who have always been somewhat intrigued by the Commandos series, but always sucked at it too much to actually pass the first mission. Don't expect anything revolutionary, though, and veterans of the genre will probably not like it as much, however it is a quick fix if you like these types of games and already finished the classics five times in a row.

[GOG profile](https://www.gog.com/u/ovoon)

My initial reaction to the price was "why would they do this?!".  But then I remembered all of the hours I got  out of this brilliant little gem.  I've beaten this game four times, and I come back to it every so often to beat it again.  The art work is gorgeous, the gameplay can get addicting and the story, while cheesy, is enjoyable.  

This is one of my favorite games, and I recommend it to anyone.

#### Commandos for impatient people

**lucastej — June 10, 2012 — 4/5**
[GOG profile](https://www.gog.com/u/lucastej)

Commandos game with better story and much more action-based. If you have no patience for quietly sneaking around and killing soldiers one by one, just forget it and go "Leeeroy Jenkins!" on them. This violates the core principle of Commandos-style games, but srsly, who cares as long it's a fun game? And I had fun playing it.

#### TOP TIER GAME

**SirArun — July 21, 2013 — 5/5**
[GOG profile](https://www.gog.com/u/SirArun)

This game is truly one of the best adventure games out there - especially if you are a fan of Robin Hood.

This is 2D graphics at its finest - the zenith of what "old games" have to offer in terms of beauty. Everything is highly detailed, and you feel immersed into medieval England as you sneak into multiple, populated castles and cities and use tactical maneuvers to get past guards.

The game also has a nice ambushing system where you boost your economy by laying traps and intercepting armed supply caravans.

Lastly, the combat is fairly awesome too, with Robin slashing his sword in the direction you move your mouse.

10/10 would definitely recommend if you love slow paced games with flair and character.

#### Decent Little Fiction-Based Gem

**GreggDelirious — March 6, 2012 — 4/5**
[GOG profile](https://www.gog.com/u/GreggDelirious)

I first discovered this game in the discount rack at T.J. Maxx a few years ago, and it really is fun. Aside from the typical strategy elements, there is a mechanic for swordplay, in which you move the mouse in a particular motion to execute different moves. 

The price is a little steep at 9.99, but if you find yourself with some extra dosh, and don't mind taking a risk, I think you'll be pleasantly surprised.
